Subject: Initial VPC / air-gapped questionnaire (Galactic Health)

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As discussed, we're assembling responses for our internal review board and need written answers to a few focused items about Redwood's private deployment model (VPC, on-prem, and air-gapped). Attached is our short questionnaire (GH-RFI-Initial.pdf).

High level asks:
- 1) How does Redwood enforce egress controls when deployed in an air-gapped environment?
- 2) What dependencies (external control plane, telemetry, licensing) require outbound connectivity, if any?
- 3) Key management recommendations and rotation windows for HSM/KMS integration.

Can you confirm you can field this in writing this week? Our procurement deadline for the first pass is 2028-03-24.

Thanks,
Priya Malhotra
Head of Security Operations
Galactic Health

Attachment: GH-RFI-Initial.pdf (questionnaire, 4 pages)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 14:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial VPC / air-gapped questionnaire (Galactic Health)

Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. We've completed a written response and attached the detailed package (20280316-galactic-rfi-answers.pdf) plus a reference network diagram (onprem-network-diagram.pdf). High-level summary here so your reviewers can triage quickly: 

- Egress controls: Redwood can run in a fully-airgapped mode. Outbound network ports are entirely configurable at deployment time. When airgapped, the control plane APIs are replaced with a local control plane that uses the same management UI but only within the customer's VPC/network. No telemetry or metrics are sent to Redwood's hosted services in that mode.

- Dependencies: In private deploy (non-airgapped), optional telemetry and health pings go to our control plane. For air-gapped/on-prem customers we provide a self-hosted control plane binary and a (signed) offline update bundle; no outbound connectivity is required for runtime.

- KMS/HSM: We support standard KMIP and cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11. Recommended rotation window is configurable; default guidance is 90 days for workload encryption keys with automated reconciliation hooks.

We've also included an appendix with our prescriptive checklist for network ACLs, host firewall rules, and allowed port lists that your infra team can paste into their change request. Marcus and Vanessa are copied in for technical detail. If you'd like, we can schedule a 45-minute walkthrough of the package next week.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20280316-galactic-rfi-answers.pdf; onprem-network-diagram.pdf

Priya —

Quick operational notes to accompany Jordan's package (pulled from the appendix):

- Patching & updates: For air-gapped installs we provide quarterly signed update bundles. Operators stage the bundle in an internal update repo; the runtime has a safe rollback policy (last-known-good). We recommend testing update bundles in a staging environment that mirrors your production VLAN segmentation.

- Day 0/1 playbook: Included in the attached RFI answers is a Day 0 checklist (DNS, NTP, cert bootstrap) and a Day 1 smoke test script (token issuance, small-batch inference, KV cache warming).

- Backup/restore: Model files and config snapshots are stored on customer-managed object storage (S3-compatible) inside the VPC. Backups can be encrypted with your KMS; please confirm whether you want Redwood-managed rotation hooks (requires outbound control-plane access) or fully-local rotation.

If you can confirm which backup pattern you prefer, I can provide the exact commands and the volume sizing guidance for initial capacity.

—Vanessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: excerpted playbook section included in 20280316-galactic-rfi-answers.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial VPC / air-gapped questionnaire (Galactic Health)

Hi Priya —

A few security-specific clarifications to add to the written answers: 

- Audit logs: When running private/offline, audit logs are written to customer-configured, append-only storage. We provide a signed checksum file for each log bundle and a log-rotation policy example.

- Secrets & signing: Support for PKCS#11 HSMs + ability to use resident keys only. We can operate with keys that never leave your HSM (no escrow).

- Key rotation: While defaults are 90 days, for high-sensitivity workloads we recommend 30-day rotation for signing keys with automated verification. We included a short attestation snapshot showing our last internal SOC2 control mapping for deployment configurations (attestation-snapshot.txt).

- Supply chain: All deployment artifacts are signed by Redwood's build service; we provide SBOM on request and can deliver a signed SBOM bundle as part of onboarding.

Happy to join a technical call to walk through any of these controls.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security Architect — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: attestation-snapshot.txt)

Jordan/Team —

Thanks for the rapid, thorough package. A few clarifying items from our infra/security reviewers before we proceed to the procurement checklist: 

- Egress control confirmation: In the diagram you shared, can you explicitly call out which services (if any) require DNS or CRL access during runtime? Our policy prohibits any DNS queries outside the VPC without exception.

- KMS flow: For PKCS#11/HSM integration, what is the recommended key rotation tooling? Do you provide built-in rotation controllers that execute inside the VPC, or do we need to run our own rotation cron?

- Attestation frequency: Will you provide periodic attestation snapshots, or are those provided on request only? We prefer scheduled monthly attestations for critical deployments.

Also — procurement asked whether the offline update bundle signing key can be rotated from our side (we don't want Redwood holding the signing key for updates).

Can we get answers to these three points by EOD Friday (2028-03-24)? If so, we can move to the initial SOW draft.

Best,
Priya

Priya/Devon —

Answers inline below and linked to the updated appendix in our shared doc: https://redwood.app/doc/gh-2028/rfi-answers (short URL included in package).

- DNS/CRL: In air-gapped mode Redwood runtime performs zero external DNS/CRL lookups by default. The only exception is an optional (customer-enabled) update-checker which is disabled in strict-airgap installs. We will add an explicit note to the diagram calling out zero external DNS by default and the controls to enable a pinned CRL endpoint if you want scheduled revocation checks via a customer-operated proxy.

- KMS rotation tooling: We provide an in-VPC rotation controller as an optional container that calls your HSM via PKCS#11 and performs rotation according to your policy. It runs inside the VPC and requires no outbound connectivity. If you prefer, you can run your own rotation process; Redwood's controller is plug-and-play and open-source so you can operate or fork it.

- Attestation frequency: We can provide scheduled attestations (monthly) as part of an enterprise addendum. By default attestations are provided on request; monthly scheduling requires a signed cadence in the SOW.

- Offline update signing key: Yes — the offline update signing key can be held by Galactic Health. Redwood will provide tooling and key format guidance to allow you to sign bundles locally. We will not retain the customer's offline signing key unless explicitly contracted.

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule a 45-minute technical handshake (Marcus + Vanessa on the call). Suggested slots: Mon 2028-03-27 10:00–10:45 PT or Tue 2028-03-28 14:00–14:45 PT. Please confirm which works for your team.
2) If monthly attestations are required, procurement and legal will need the small enterprise addendum — I can circulate a draft SOW after the call.
